title: bn254-pairing-inversion: distinguished-point rho on Frobenius classes, output ([x]P0, Q0)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and z=g^x in the protected BN254 target group GT, with g=e(P0,Q0), the algorithm in proof.md (sequential distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT: 2^14 twisted multipliers, a 4-multiplication class selector, a 24-class look-back window with up to 8 probes, 87 distinguished bits, an ordered store of canonical exponents and the check g^x=z, then output of P=[x]P0 in G1 and Q=Q0 in G2) returns points P and Q with e(P,Q)=z with success at least 0.39, as algorithmic probability over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, under the disclosed heuristics H1 (the class walk behaves like a random mapping within factor mu=6/5), H2 (hash fields and twist increments of distinct classes behave as independent uniform values) and H3 (tie rate), supported by algebra on the pinned constants and full-algorithm toy runs. The step budget S_max is the least integer whose square is at least 2(6/5)N ln(5/3), N=(r-1)/12. Total computation is at most 2^124.763426 target-group-operation equivalents (scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C=20,000) on every run, with no run gate. This cap is enforced by meters: 15,267 executed instructions per slot (13,843 for the Fp12 product, 1,067 for the class selector and 357 for the remaining per-slot work, all generated AArch64 programs) times S_max+floor(S_max/2^13)+1+2^94 slots, plus all input checks, constants, table construction, fresh coins (16 instructions per 64-bit word), trail starts, reports, store operations, recoveries, verification, the scalar multiplication of the output and an attack-side pairing check. Peak memory is at most 2^47.000001 bytes in one address space below 2^48; preprocessing is at most 2^23.478998 equivalents and is included in the run total; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The identity input z=1 returns P=infinity (null) and Q=Q0, as the rules permit exactly for z=1. Nothing is amortised over other targets, and no prior acceptance, submission or score is a premise. Analytic exploratory claim: no production-size run, not a finite-field sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Generate and execute the priced AArch64 programs (Fp multiply/add/sub, Fp12 product, class selector) against big-integer arithmetic and print executed counts; check the algebra on the pinned BN254 constants; recompute every ledger integer, the score and the trap sums; execute the output step P=[x]P0 with counted field operations against an independent affine reference; run the complete algorithm of proof.md in the BN-family toy field q=p(-15), r'=r(-15). Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
